An abandoned camp, one of many spread all along the coast. Most camps are abandoned and a mess left behind like this.

They often leave edible food behind, canned, bottled, or packaged. They are scavengers. Mostly they leave behind garbage that they have scavenged from the area.

This particular camp is infested with spiders, but they seem friendly. Just entering the area into the trees you cannot help to be scratching all over, and into the night.

This particular camp is unique, as it holds several stashes of materials. 

Notice the close up photo of the gasoline powered bicycle stashed away made to look like a big rats nest but partially uncovered.

The ultimate minimalist world touring machine. Everyone needs one. Not everyone wants one. Some dream of them, while others would never dare to dream. 

Fully equipped to do and go just about anywhere, depending on the extremes. Uniquely put together by each one of us, can't be bought in stores.

This version, 7k usd, includes one week of real-time stealth touring lessons.

Two of many different treasures to be found in the thousands of dumpsters in this area that America's most wealthy students use to dispose of their unwanted possessions. 

Yesterday I found 10 kilos of packaged cheese and another 10 kilos of butter, among many other things.

Waste continues to be a way of life in parts of America.  What I  photograph to show here is only 1% of what I witness.

It's a shame, a disgrace. This generation or the next will pay a price.

Minimalistic zero-waste life under a tree along the southern California coast implemented through modern technology. Not a glamorous life, but it's really all we need. The treasures to be found among the discards of this wasteful and uncaring generation will someday end, and people will need to learn to live without. 

How can anyone justify their own consumption habits without taking into account the injustices of uneven distribution? The rich live flagrantly while the poor struggle for their very survival. 

And who are these rich celebrities and superstars that serve as role models? How can they justify the images of consumerism they represent in movies, the media, and advertising?
Life under a hot Indian chai, with tea in the morning, and a wide variety of discarded healthy and fresh foods always to found everyday.
